To keep using oil, a valuable resource and limited resource is coming to an end for Iran.

The Government has decided to do away with fossil fuels to power Iran and to keep it moving.

Hydrogen was selected as it successor due to recharge speed and because it will become the main supplier of the Iranian Military.

Building the Hydrogen Economy and the Hydrogen infrastructure will take time and a ton of money but by doing so Iran will be the first country in the world to have a full renewable energy consumption and production. And Iran hopes that by doing so that they are a peaceful nation who looks towards the future of not only itself but also those of the other nations.

The plan is to finish the transition to the Hydrogen Economy by 2038, over the course of 10 years during which the costly subsidies will be removed over the 10 year process,

The Subsidies are costing Iran around $100.000.000.000 a year in lost taxes and a lot of potentially lost oil revenue

_____

**The Infrastructure**

To succeed in building a hydrogen economy, the infrastructure is vital to it, pipelines need to be laid, building need to be connected to it, vehicles need a place to refuel.

Iran chose for a centralized production scheme to be able to benefit from massive economies of scale with massive amounts of underground pipelines providing Hydrogen gas to every building in Iran from the Urban areas to the most remote buildings.

To allow the Iranians to use the Hydrogen that will be connected to their house or building. they will get a free stove and a free central heating station installed which are powered by Hydrogen.

Of course as a result there can be no more fossil fuels vehicles on the roads and to replace them hydrogen fuel cell factories will need to be built to provide the fuel cells needed at a low cost, which is estimated to be at $20 per KW.

Existing Car Factories will be converted to produce hydrogen powered vehicles using the previously mention fuel cells.

Cars cannot drive without fuel and need to be refueled regularly, and so there needs to be plenty of refueling stations across the country. A large number of refueling stations will be built to be able to provide vehicles with the hydrogen that is needed.

________

**The Production**

Currently Iran uses 2.000.000 barrels of oil a day and 144.6 billion cubic meter of natural gas.

It is estimated that Iran would need around 80.000.000.000 KG of Hydrogen a year to replace the oil and Natural gas and 50% for future increase in consumption and for additional production capabilities. And some additional hydrogen factories to ensure steady supply while a plant is down for maintenance.

To produce the amount required the only viable option is Nuclear Hydrogen production using 4th Generation Nuclear Reactors which are especially designed for hydrogen production.

Although Iran did not initially possess this reactor type, Iran contacted South Korea to purchase the reactor design and successfully negotiated a deal for the reactor design which benefits both South Korea and Iran.

Building Hydrogen Factories off 500 Mwh would allow for an optimal investment per factory and production capabilities

A Nuclear Hydrogen Factory would produce 135.000 Tons of Hydrogen per day, at that rate with allowing for future production and downtime of factories. Iran would require 5 of the 500 Mwh size Nuclear Hydrogen Factories, 2 will be built by South Korea as the price for the reactor design and training our staff for technology transfer, the remaining 3 will be built by Iran.

The cost of Hydrogen per kilogram is estimated to be $0.75, due to using the latest 4th Generation nuclear reactor and economies of scale.

Of course to produce Hydrogen you need fresh water, it was decided to use desalinated water instead of fresh water or taken from the existing infrastructure as to relief the already strained water infrastructure. At 100% efficiency 9 liters of water would be required for each Kg of Hydrogen. Therefor an estimated 1.080.000.000.000 liters of water would be required to get the hydrogen that would be required which would require 5 desalination plants running continuously without allowing any time for maintenance or any unexpected interruption. And thus 8 Nuclear Desalination plants will be built to supply the Nuclear Hydrogen Plants with excess water being sent in the water network as it is perfectly clean drinking water. The electricity produced in the desalination process will be added to the electricity network.

_____

**The Final Push**

There are still fossil fuel power plants including emergency diesel power plants that will need to be decommissioned and replaced. Currently there are 30088 MWh Fossil Powered Power Plants that will need to be replaced by non-fossil fuel powered power plants and 118 MWh installed for emergency uses.

Hydrogen powered power plants will be the emergency power supply, 4 of such plants will be installed with a total capacity of 1000 MWh for emergency power.

To replace the 30088 MWh it was decided to use solar energy, 7 gigantic solar farms will be constructed with each a capacity of 5000 MWh.

These Gigantic Solar Power Plants will be able to provide Iran with the energy needed to replace the Fossil Fuel Powered Power Plants.
